videos.subject: Why you choose healthy food for later, but not now 🍎
videos.script: You're more likely to pick fruit for later, and chocolate for now. Two hundred workers chose a snack they'd get a week later. Many chose an apple or a banana. A week later, they could choose again, right then. Far more took chips or a chocolate bar. Future you eats well. Right-now you doesn't. That's why
videos.hook_text: Snack for next week: fruit or chocolate?

videos.subject: Why you stick with the box that's already checked ☑️
videos.script: You'll say yes far more often when yes is already checked. In an online study, people chose whether to be organ donors. When they had to check a box to join, far fewer joined. When they were in unless they unchecked it, about twice as many stayed in. The default chose for them. That's why

videos.subject: What happens if you let a coin flip decide? 🪙
videos.script: Letting a coin push you to change was linked to more happiness. In over twenty thousand coin flips, people stuck on a choice, like quitting a job, let a coin decide. Heads meant: make the change. Heads made them far more likely to do it. Six months later, the changers were happier, on average. So
videos.hook_text: Quit or stay? Flip a coin.
